# Meet the Winners of the 2024 Goodreads Choice Awards
Posted by Cybil on December 4, 2024 
[104 likes](https://www.goodreads.com/rating/voters/2879?resource_type=Blog) · [48 comments](https://www.goodreads.com/blog/show/2879-meet-the-winners-of-the-2024-goodreads-choice-awards#top)
Share
[![](https://images.gr-assets.com/misc/1731606727-1731606727_goodreads_misc.png)](https://www.goodreads.com/choiceawards/best-books-2024)
The 16th Annual Goodreads Choice Awards are now official! With a new record of more than 6.2 million votes cast, the 2024 awards continue the Goodreads tradition of honoring readers’ favorite books of the year.  
  
This time around, we’ve got 15 separate categories with 300 nominated books total. You can find the winners in each listed below, along with a link to all the nominated books in that category.  
  
Alert readers will note that several returning winners are featured this year. [Emily Henry](https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/13905555.Emily_Henry "https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/13905555.Emily_Henry") scored her fourth Readers’ Favorite Romance win in a row with  _[Funny Story](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/194803835-funny-story "https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/194803835-funny-story")_ (soon to be a movie, [apparently](https://variety.com/2024/film/news/funny-story-movie-emily-henry-writing-1236063486/ "https://variety.com/2024/film/news/funny-story-movie-emily-henry-writing-1236063486/")). [Stephen King](https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/3389.Stephen_King "https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/3389.Stephen_King")’s short fiction collection  _[You Like It Darker](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/201242757-you-like-it-darker "https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/201242757-you-like-it-darker")_ took the Horror prize, giving King a total of 11 career wins across four categories over the years.   
  
Other returning winners include [Kristin Hannah](https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/54493.Kristin_Hannah "https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/54493.Kristin_Hannah"), [T.J. ## Biography
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alison_Espach&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]
Espach was born in [Trumbull, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trumbull,_Connecticut "Trumbull, Connecticut"), on September 26, 1984.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-Patch_2011-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-2) She is a 2007 graduate of [Providence College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College") in [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), Rhode Island, where English professor [Peter Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Johnson_\(poet\) "Peter Johnson \(poet\)") was a mentor.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-PC_News_2016-3)
After graduation, she pursued a [Master of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Fine_Arts "Master of Fine Arts") at [Washington University in St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_University_in_St._Louis "Washington University in St. Louis"), Missouri, during which she wrote a thesis that would become her first novel, _The Adults_ (2011). She moved to New York to teach writing after completing the program.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-Patch_2011-1) In 2013, she joined the faculty of Providence College.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-PC_News_2016-3) She is a professor of English.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Espach#cite_note-4)

# Bantam Lake: The Largest (Natural) Lake
November 4, 2008 by [Steve](https://www.ctmq.org/author/steve/) [3 Comments](https://www.ctmq.org/the-largest-natural-lake/#comments)
**This Lake is no Bantam Weight  
Bantam Lake, Litchfield/Morris**  
November 2, 2008
[Re-reading this page now in 2013, it’s very Wiki-heavy. Sorry about that.]
Bantam? What of this Bantam? While separated for census and historic reasons, Bantam is governed as an integral part of the town of Litchfield. Bantam is the 2nd least populous borough in Connecticut, only beaten by Fenwick and is the 3rd least populous municipality in Connecticut only beaten by Union and Fenwick.
![](https://www.ctmq.org/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2008/11/bantam.jpg)
Fenwick? What of this Fenwick? Fenwick is a borough in Middlesex County in the town of [Old Saybrook](https://www.ctmq.org/ctmqs-guide-to-old-saybrook/). The population was 52 at the 2000 census. It is considered one of the most prestigious summer colonies in the country.
Oh. I had never heard of it before beginning CTMQ. Not that I’d heard of Bantam either. Not until I found out that the largest natural lake was there. The CTMQ Family was lucky enough to check out the lake during a 4 winery tour in Litchfield County. We actually drove very near the largest lake in the state – Lake Candlewood – but didn’t stop. Bah, that lake is phony baloney man-made anyway. Natural is always my preference… In women, fruit flavors, and lakes.
![](https://www.ctmq.org/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2008/11/__0008.jpg)
Bantam Lake is quite popular with boaters and especially water-skiers. In fact, the Bantam Ski Club is the oldest continuous waterski club in the country! (Awesome photo of some members above.) We passed its headquarters along North Shore Drive and noticed that it, along with many other tiny little chalets there, evoke a sort of misplaced Alpine feel somehow. 
Yes Bantam Lake is the largest natural lake in Connecticut, with a surface area of 930 acres with a maximum depth of 23 feet. Much of the land at the Northern end of the lake, including the peninsula of Marsh Point, is protected by White Memorial Foundation and this area is home to a wide array of bird species.
